content.text: {"grade": 6, "complete": false, "main_gap": "The constructive half of the Refinement Lemma (Xiang achieving D \u2264 \u0393 with \u2264 q\u22121 cuts) is only sketched: the overlay pairing and the crucial cut-count |A|+|B|\u22121+(q\u2212|A|\u2212|B|)=q\u22121 are asserted, 'details omitted'.", "errors": [{"description": "Upper-bound half of the refinement lemma: the overlay/common-refinement construction and, critically, the claim that it uses at most q\u22121 cuts are stated without proof. This step is essential for the upper bound c \u2264 2^n/(2^{n+1}\u22121); it is verifiable and tight, but as written it is an unproved assertion.", "quote": "and use at most \\(q-1\\) cuts in total (standard; details omitted)."}, {"description": "The 56-unit 'grid example' is presented as agreeing with the theorem, but Liu's intervals (7,14,35) have \u0393=7/56=1/8, so optimal Xiang play holds Liu to 9/16 < 4/7; the displayed Xiang moves (8,38) are simply suboptimal. The claimed 'agreement' is misleading (though only offered as evidence, not proof).", "quote": "Sorting gives Liu\n\\((18+13+1)/56=32/56=4/7\\), in agreement with the theorem."}, {"description": "Minor: in the lower-bound graph argument, the exclusion of loops from the chosen tree component (needed since a loop edge would contribute \u00b1(x_{2j-1}+x_{2j}) rather than \u00b1(x_{2j-1}\u2212x_{2j})) is not spelled out, although it follows from e_C=v_C\u22121 with connectivity.", "quote": "Loops and parallel edges are allowed."}], "notes": "Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}\u22121) and the main structure (greedy drafting value (1+D)/2; D_min = minimal subset-sum gap; pigeonhole; binary construction) are correct, and the graph-theoretic lower-bound half is fully rigorous. Only the constructive half is left unproved."}
